records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י ע֚וֹד לֵ֣ךְ אֱֽהַב־אִשָּׁ֔ה אֲהֻ֥בַת רֵ֖עַ וּמְנָאָ֑פֶת כְּאַהֲבַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהֵ֗ם פֹּנִים֙ אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְאֹהֲבֵ֖י אֲשִׁישֵׁ֥י עֲנָבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, Again go, love a woman loved of a companion and committing adultery, like [the] love of Yahweh [for] the sons of Israel, and they [are] turning to gods other and loving cakes of raisins.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves the people of Israel, though they turn to other gods and love raisin cakes."

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Again go, love a woman loved by a companion and committing adultery, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, while they are turning to other gods and loving cakes of raisins."

R.1: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Go again and love a woman who has another lover and is unfaithful to her husband. Love her the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves the people of Israel, even though they turn to other gods and love the raisin cakes offered to them."

decisions.choice: a woman: most likely Gomer, though the text does not name her
alternatives: the marriage of chapter 1, told again by Hosea
decisions.reason: The chapter is told by Hosea himself ("to me"). The woman is not named. Most readers take her to be Gomer: "again" points back to chapter 1, and the picture requires the LORD to love the same people who have been unfaithful to him, so Hosea must love the wife who has been unfaithful to him. Others take her to be a second woman, or read chapter 3 as Hosea's own account of the marriage in chapter 1. The text leaves the woman unnamed.

decisions.choice: loved by a companion: loved by another man; possibly by her husband
decisions.reason: The word means a friend, a companion or a neighbor, and in Jeremiah 3:20 it is used of a husband. "Loved by another man" fits the words that follow, "and committing adultery". Some read "loved by her husband", which would make the point that she is loved by Hosea and yet unfaithful. The reading "another man" is taken here.

decisions.choice: again: the LORD speaks again, and Hosea is to go again
decisions.reason: "Again" stands between "said to me" and "go" and can belong to either: "the LORD said to me again" or "go again". Both point back to chapter 1. Placed with "go", it says that Hosea is to love again.

decisions.choice: raisin cakes: festival food, here tied to the worship of other gods
decisions.reason: Cakes of pressed raisins were a festival food; David gave them to the people when the ark came to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:19). Here they go with the worship of other gods, as offerings or as food eaten at their feasts. Compare the cakes baked for the queen of heaven in Jeremiah 7:18.

decisions.choice: as the LORD loves the people of Israel: Hosea's love is to mirror the LORD's
decisions.reason: The command is not only to take the woman back but to love her, as the LORD keeps loving a people who turn to other gods. The love comes first; the change in her comes later (3:3-5).

decisions.choice: has another lover (R); unfaithful to her husband (R); offered to them (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "loved by a companion and committing adultery" means (m2) and that the raisin cakes belong to the worship of the other gods (m4). It does not say whose wife she is, which the text leaves open (m1).

records.heading: Go again and love

records.source: וָאֶכְּרֶ֣הָ לִּ֔י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר כָּ֑סֶף וְחֹ֥מֶר שְׂעֹרִ֖ים וְלֵ֥תֶךְ שְׂעֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I bought her for myself for fifteen silver and a homer of barley and a lethech of barley.
pieces: So I bought her for myself for {{units:about 6 ounces of silver|fifteen shekels of silver}} and {{units:about 9 bushels of barley|a homer and a lethech of barley}}.

L.2: So I bought her for myself for fifteen [shekels of] silver and a homer of barley and a lethech of barley.

R.2: So I paid {{units:about 6 ounces of silver|fifteen shekels of silver}} and {{units:about 9 bushels of barley|a homer and a lethech of barley}} to get her for myself.

decisions.choice: bought her: acquired her by paying a price
decisions.reason: The verb is used for buying or bargaining (Deuteronomy 2:6). The verse does not say whom Hosea paid or why. She may have become someone's slave, or bound to another man, or the payment may be a bride-price for a new marriage. The price shows that bringing her back cost him something.

decisions.choice: fifteen shekels of silver, a homer and a lethech of barley: a price paid partly in silver, partly in grain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "fifteen silver", meaning fifteen shekels; a shekel weighed about two-fifths of an ounce. A homer was about 6 bushels, the same measure used in Ezekiel 45:11. The lethech is named only here; it is usually taken as half a homer. Paying partly in barley, the cheapest grain, may suggest that Hosea did not have the whole sum in silver. The Greek translation reads "a measure of wine" instead of the lethech of barley.

decisions.choice: about 6 ounces of silver; about 9 bushels of barley (units setting)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew units and supplies "shekels of". Balanced and Readable give modern measures by default, with the original units as the alternative. The homer and lethech are given together, about 6 and 3 bushels, since the lethech is taken as half a homer (m2).

decisions.choice: So I paid ... to get her for myself
decisions.reason: Readable puts the price first and the purpose after, which reads more easily than "bought her for ...".

records.source: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלֶ֗יהָ יָמִ֤ים רַבִּים֙ תֵּ֣שְׁבִי לִ֔י לֹ֣א תִזְנִ֔י וְלֹ֥א תִֽהְיִ֖י לְאִ֑ישׁ וְגַם־אֲנִ֖י אֵלָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And I said to her, Days many you will stay for me; not you will prostitute yourself, and not you will be for a man; and also I to you.
pieces: Then I said to her, "You must stay with me for many days. You must not prostitute yourself or belong to any man, and I will do the same toward you."

L.3: And I said to her, "Many days you will stay for me; you will not prostitute yourself, and you will not be for a man; and I also [will be so] toward you."

R.3: I told her, "You must live with me for a long time. You must not be unfaithful or be with any man. And I will do the same for you."

decisions.choice: and I also toward you: Hosea will keep the same restraint toward her
alternatives: and I will not come to you either
decisions.reason: The last words are only "and also I to you". They most likely mean that Hosea too will wait, keeping himself from relations with her for the same time, as 3:4 pictures Israel living without the things it leaned on. They could also mean "and I will be yours", a promise that he will be faithful to her.

decisions.choice: stay for me many days ... not be for a man: a time of waiting, apart from all lovers
decisions.reason: "Many days" is a long time with no end named. To "be for a man" means to belong to him as a wife or lover (Deuteronomy 24:2). She is to live set apart, belonging to no other man, while she waits.

decisions.choice: prostitute yourself: be unfaithful
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:2 and 2:7 for unfaithfulness, set for Hosea as "prostitute oneself" at Literal and Balanced and "be unfaithful" at Readable.

decisions.choice: stay with me (B); live with me (R); belong to any man (B); be with any man (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idioms mean (m2). Readable says "a long time" for "many days". The last clause is kept close to the Hebrew at every level, so that the footnote's question stays open (m1).

records.source: כִּ֣י׀יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים יֵֽשְׁבוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֥ין מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ וְאֵ֣ין שָׂ֔ר וְאֵ֥ין זֶ֖בַח וְאֵ֣ין מַצֵּבָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין אֵפ֖וֹד וּתְרָפִֽים׃
records.gloss: For days many will stay [the] sons of Israel without king and without prince and without sacrifice and without pillar and without ephod and teraphim.
pieces: For the people of Israel will live for many days with no king or prince, no sacrifice or sacred pillar, no ephod or household gods.

L.4: For many days the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel will stay with no king and no prince, and no sacrifice and no pillar, and no ephod and teraphim.

R.4: In the same way, the people of Israel will live for a long time with no king or ruler, with no sacrifices or sacred stones, and with no ephod or household idols.

decisions.choice: for ... will stay: the woman's waiting pictures Israel's
decisions.reason: "For" ties the verse to the one before. The woman "stays" many days (3:3), and Israel "will stay" many days: the same verb. Her time apart is a sign of what Israel will go through.

decisions.choice: pillar, ephod, teraphim: objects of worship and of seeking guidance
decisions.reason: A sacred pillar was a standing stone set up at a shrine (Genesis 28:18), later forbidden because of its use in the worship of other gods (Deuteronomy 16:22; 2 Kings 17:10). An ephod was a priestly garment, used when seeking an answer from God (1 Samuel 23:9-12), and sometimes an object of worship (Judges 8:27; 17:5). Teraphim were household images, used in divination (Genesis 31:19; 1 Samuel 19:13; Ezekiel 21:26).

decisions.choice: without king, prince, sacrifice: Israel deprived of its government and its worship, lawful and unlawful alike
decisions.reason: The list joins things the law allowed (king, sacrifice, ephod) with things it condemned (pillar, teraphim). All are taken away. This describes the exile, when Israel would have neither its rulers nor its shrines.

decisions.choice: sacred pillar (B); sacred stones (R); household gods (B); household idols (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "pillar" and "teraphim". Balanced and Readable say what they were (m2). "Ephod" has no ordinary English equivalent and is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: In the same way
decisions.reason: Readable says how this verse is linked to the last (m1).

records.source: אַחַ֗ר יָשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבִקְשׁוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת דָּוִ֣ד מַלְכָּ֑ם וּפָחֲד֧וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֛ה וְאֶל־טוּב֖וֹ בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִֽים׃פ
records.gloss: Afterward will return [the] sons of Israel and they will seek Yahweh their God and David their king, and they will come trembling to Yahweh and to his goodness at [the] end of the days.
pieces: Afterward the people of Israel will turn back and seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God and David their king. In days to come they will come trembling to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} goodness.

L.5: Afterward the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel will return, and they will seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God and David their king; and they will come trembling to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} goodness at the end of the days.

R.5: After that, the people of Israel will come back. They will look for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God and for their king from David's family. In the future they will come to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} trembling with awe, to receive the good things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives.

decisions.choice: David their king: a king from David's line
decisions.reason: David had died long before Hosea. As in Jeremiah 30:9 and Ezekiel 34:23-24; 37:24-25, "David" means a king of David's family who will rule as David did. The northern kingdom had broken away from David's house (1 Kings 12:16); its return means coming back under that line, as Judah and Israel are joined under one head in 2:2. Jewish and Christian readers have long seen in this king the Messiah, the anointed son of David.

decisions.choice: return and seek: turn back to the LORD and look to him
decisions.reason: "Return" is the word Hosea uses for repentance, turning back to God (6:1; 14:2). To "seek" the LORD is to turn to him in worship and need (5:15). The same verb was used for the woman seeking her lovers (2:9).

decisions.choice: come trembling: come in awe and eagerness
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to tremble with fear. With "to the LORD" it means coming to him with awe, in eager reverence (compare Micah 7:17; Isaiah 60:5, where the heart "trembles" with joy). The people come shaken but drawn.

decisions.choice: his goodness ... at the end of the days: the good gifts of the LORD in the time to come
decisions.reason: "His goodness" is the LORD's kindness and the good things he gives, like the grain, wine and oil of Jeremiah 31:12, 14. "The end of the days" means the time to come, not necessarily the end of the world (Isaiah 2:2). Deuteronomy 4:30 uses the same words: "in the end of the days you will return to the LORD your God".

decisions.choice: in days to come (B); in the future (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as Isaiah 2:2 at each level.

decisions.choice: their king from David's family (R); trembling with awe (R); the good things he gives (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that "David" means a king of David's family, as in Jeremiah 30:9 (m1), and says what the trembling and the goodness mean (m3, m4).
